correctness.rationale: The base subset sums for {2,...,4} are {0,2,3,4,5,6,7,9}, and induction by adjoining m+1 shows exactly {0,T_m-1} union [2,T_m-3]. Star chords ensure every q in [3,T_m-2] is the connected sum 1+subset(2..m). For b=m+2..n the extra spoke {1,m+2} joins the cycle tail with a star subset and yields I_b=[H_b+3,H_b+T_m-2]. Consecutive I_b cover the entire middle range since n<=T_m-4; singleton vertex labels cover 1..m+4 and the full cycle or removal of r<=m+2 covers T_n-m-2..T_n. No gap remains; n>=9 gives 4<=m<=n-4 so chords are genuine and distinct. Independently enumerated all 2^n-1 vertex subsets and checked connected weights for n=9..14, matching every target integer and chord count; theorem for all n follows induction and interval bounds, not enumeration.
residual_risks: The formula is an upper bound and leaves the exact minimum and optimal growth rate unknown.
Finite subset census n<=14 does not establish the infinite result.

final_claim: For every n>=9, m=min{r>=4:T_r>=n+4}, adding m-1 chords {1,j} (3<=j<=m) and {1,m+2} makes every integer 1..T_n the sum of a nonempty connected induced vertex set, hence mEC(n)<=ceil((sqrt(8n+33)-1)/2)-1=√(2n)+O(1) and mEC(n)/n→0.
